title: Sequential Spinodal Decompositions and Ordering Reactions in an As-Quenched Cr<sub>39</sub>Co<sub>18</sub>Fe<sub>18</sub>Ni<sub>18</sub>Al<sub>7</sub> High-Entropy Alloy.

recollection.starting_material: Guess: A solutionized single-phase FCC high-entropy alloy of nominal composition Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 that was homogenized at high temperature (~1100–1200 C) and water-quenched to retain a supersaturated solid solution.
recollection.intervention: Guess: Rapid quench from the high-temperature single-phase field, followed by isothermal aging in the 450–700 C range; microstructural evolution characterized by atom probe tomography, STEM/HRTEM with EDS, XRD/SAED, and differential scanning calorimetry to resolve spinodal modulations and ordering.
recollection.structure: Guess: A hierarchical microstructure forming in the as-quenched/low-temperature-aged state: (i) a primary nanoscale FCC spinodal modulation separating a Cr-rich network from a (Ni,Co,Fe,Al)-rich network with an initial wavelength of ~2–4 nm, and (ii) subsequent ordering within the (Ni,Co,Fe,Al)-rich regions to form L12-type gamma'-like ordered domains; at longer times or higher temperatures, limited emergence of a Cr-rich bcc-like alpha' phase while the FCC matrix persists.
recollection.mechanism: Guess: First, chemical spinodal decomposition driven by positive Cr–Ni/Co mixing enthalpies yields a Cr-enriched and a Ni/Co/Fe-enriched FCC network. Al partitions strongly to the Ni/Co/Fe-rich side. Second, Ni–Al-driven ordering within those Al-enriched channels produces L12 short- to long-range order (Ni3(Al,Fe,Co)-like). A possible secondary spinodal within the Cr-rich network or continued ordering in the Ni/Co/Fe-rich network leads to sequential, hierarchical modulations. Coarsening is sluggish and influenced by elastic and compositional coupling.
recollection.results: Guess: Primary spinodal wavelength ~2–3 nm in the as-quenched state, increasing to ~5–7 nm after 1–10 h at ~600 C. Compositional partitioning measured by APT shows Cr rising to ~60–70 at% in the Cr-rich regions, with Al enrichment factors of ~3–5 in the Ni/Co/Fe-rich regions that order. L12-like ordered volume fraction ~10–20% at intermediate aging, with corresponding increases in microhardness from ~200 HV to ~350–450 HV. Diffuse/superlattice reflections in XRD/SAED consistent with L12 ordering; no substantial sigma formation in the early/intermediate stages under those conditions.

score.note: The recollection incorrectly proposes low-temperature aging of an FCC alloy; the study instead annealed at 1100–1300 °C and water-quenched. It also misidentifies the reciprocal BCC/B2 hierarchy as an FCC/L12 structure. The general sequence of spinodal decomposition followed by Ni–Al-driven ordering is directionally correct, but the phases and detailed pathway are wrong. Reported wavelengths, compositions, volume fractions, and hardness values do not match the paper.
